channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Genome Biology, Genome Research, and Molecular Cell.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Replicative gaps in DNA damage tolerance, genome instability, and cancer therapy
item.description: Replicative single-stranded DNA gaps arise when DNA synthesis proceeds past lesions or difficult-to-replicate regions. This review delineates the pathways that generate, stabilize, and process these intermediates and discusses how their persistence drives fork degradation, genome instability, innate immune activation, and altered responses to DNA damage response-targeted therapies.

item.title: Genome Biology: Phase separation of β-catenin assembles active loop hubs in colorectal cancer
Genome Biology: Sex chromosome evolution mediated by a large inversion and a possible switch of the sex determination gene
Molecular Cell: LENG8 mediates RNA nuclear retention and degradation in eukaryotes
item.description: Tian et al. identify LENG8 as a conserved RNA quality-control factor that prevents nuclear export of misprocessed mRNAs and noncoding RNAs. This study provides fundamental insight into how the surveillance machinery monitors RNA processing status to determine nuclear retention, degradation, or export.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Paraspeckle condensation is controlled via TDP-43 polymerization and linked to neuroprotection
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 18 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01895-y Hodgson, Huang, Lang et al. show that TDP-43 limits ribonucleoprotein particle condensation into paraspeckles in a concentration- and polymerization-dependent manner. They also link paraspeckle condensation to stress response and neuroprotection.

item.title: Genome Biology: Dynamic and cell-type specific transcriptional reprogramming underlies the floral transition in the maize shoot apical meristem
Nature Cell Biology: Kinase KEY1 controls pyrenoid condensate size throughout the cell cycle by disrupting phase separation interactions
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 17 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01908-w He et al. identify a central regulator of condensate size and dynamics in the Chlamydomonas CO2-fixing condensate, the pyrenoid. KEY1 phosphorylates EPYC1, a linker protein for Rubisco, to maintain pyrenoid size and number through the cell cycle.

item.title: Genome Biology: Using reciprocally retained gene families to detect whole-genome multiplications in plants
Nature Cell Biology: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate couples glycolytic activity to cell adhesion
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 16 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01911-1 Hoffmann et al. show that the glycolytic intermediate fructose-1,6-bisphosphate, which accumulates in the absence of aldolase, regulates focal adhesions by relieving RCC2-mediated Rac1 inhibition.

item.title: Genome Biology: Centromere evolution in annual and perennial soybeans and its implication for hybridization in cultivated species
Molecular Cell: Microhomology-mediated end joining acts directly on replication forks to repair single-ended double-strand breaks
item.description: Li et al. uncover a new mechanism, fork-MMEJ, at broken replication forks that repairs seDSBs with characteristics distinct from the canonical MMEJ (cMMEJ). This study provides insights into replication-associated DSB repair, implicates microhomology-mediated chromosomal rearrangements in cancer, and offers potential therapeutic strategies to selectively target cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Of rigor and outreach, and practicing what we teach
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01914-y Aditi U. Gurkar is an associate professor at the Aging Institute of the University of Pittsburgh, studying the mechanisms of ageing. We reached out to Aditi to discuss her career, perspective on the cellular ageing field, outreach efforts, and how to practice what we teach when it comes to longevity-promoting practices.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Emerging mechanisms of genome degradation during the mtDNA life cycle
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01903-1 Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is not static but undergoes a regulated ‘life cycle’ that encompasses replication, maintenance, spatial distribution and turnover. Here, we update emerging mtDNA degradative pathways, discuss the interplay between mtDNA quality control and heteroplasmy, and outline crucial questions that place the mtDNA life cycle at the forefront of mitochondrial biology.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: An SP110–SP100 axis is a critical regulator of promyelocytic leukaemia body dynamics and mitotic fidelity
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01916-w Aird et al. report that promyelocytic leukaemia (PML)-localized speckled protein 110 (SP110) controls SP100 oligomerization, which then regulates the mitotic dissolution of nuclear PML bodies.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Time-resolved functional genomics using deep learning reveals global hierarchical control of autophagy
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-025-01837-0 Chica et al. combined genetic network mapping, time-resolved imaging and deep learning to generate a dataset called AutoDRY that describes multilayered control of autophagy and uncovers new regulatory pathways.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Riboflavin metabolism shapes FSP1-driven ferroptosis resistance
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-025-01856-x After performing a focused CRISPR–Cas9 screen, Skafar et al. identify riboflavin (vitamin B2) as a regulator of FSP1 stability that modulates phospholipid peroxidation and ferroptosis sensitivity in cancer cells.

item.title: Genome Biology: Systematic evaluation of single-cell multimodal data integration enhances cell type resolution and discovery of clinically relevant states in complex tissues
Molecular Cell: Molecular basis for dual-spacer-guided target cleavage by the TIGR-TasH system
item.description: Yang et al. presented the molecular basis of the TIGR-TasH system, including autonomous precursor tigRNA processing by the Nop domain, tigRNA-dependent dimerization, lysine-triggered dsDNA unzipping, and β-hairpin-mediated recruitment of the HNH nuclease. Engineering Box C mutants enable the rational design of tigRNA-defined nickases for gene editing in mammalian cells.
